Why Small Models Win at the Edge

Running a model on a phone, a camera, or a factory sensor changes the engineering problem completely. Latency, power draw, and privacy matter more than leaderboard scores, and a model with a few hundred million parameters can often meet all three requirements where a giant model cannot.

Latency is a product feature

When a request has to travel to a data centre and back, the user waits for the network as much as for the model. On-device inference removes that round trip entirely, so responses feel instant even on a poor connection. For interactive features such as keyboard suggestions or voice commands, this difference is what users actually notice.

Quantization in one paragraph

Quantization stores each weight with fewer bits, for example eight bits instead of sixteen. The model becomes smaller and faster, and in many cases loses only a little accuracy. The right level of quantization is something you measure on your own task rather than assume.

What to measure

  • End-to-end latency on the target device
  • Peak memory during inference
  • Accuracy on your own evaluation set
  • Battery impact over a realistic session

The teams that succeed at the edge treat these four numbers as release criteria, in the same way a web team treats page load time. Everything else is secondary to whether the feature feels fast and keeps working when the network does not.
